methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Foundry Lab is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $15M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—including robotics specialists such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $15M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $30M. Peer-median analysis references four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B and a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in robotics valuations across seed and Series B stages.

The triangulated range spans $26M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $865M. This wide band reflects material tension between stage-progression and peer-median methods, indicating substantial valuation uncertainty. The peer-median approach anchors to later-stage companies; downward adjustment is warranted given Foundry Lab's Series A status. Key uncertainties include the company's differentiation within a crowded subsector, revenue traction, and timeline to Series B. A defensible range of $75M–$300M appears more consistent with Series A positioning, though further diligence on unit economics and market penetration is required.
